checking that a file is acceptable before use
the type of upload, such as a schedule or a package

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for upload page
sections.what: Brings in drag-and-drop types, the hero graphic and its styles, the validation checks for attachments, schedules and packages, and the size formatter.
sections.why: Likely reason: the page checks files locally before sending them.
sections.watch_out: The rules themselves live in another file, so this file alone does not show what is accepted.

sections.name: UploadView (part 1)
sections.title: Choosing a schedule or package to analyse
sections.what: Shows the landing text and the explanation of evidence levels, then the upload panel. The user picks Schedule or Project package, then chooses a file by clicking or by dropping it onto the drop area. Switching the type clears the chosen file.
sections.why: Likely reason: a schedule and a ZIP package need different checks, so the old file is cleared to avoid sending a file that does not fit the new type.
sections.watch_out: Dropping a file skips any type check in this handler, so the validation message and the disabled Analyse button are the only guard.

sections.name: UploadView (part 2)
sections.title: Submit button and optional extra files
sections.what: Shows the chosen file's name, size and validation message, then the Analyse button, an optional demo button, and optional extra schedules and project documents for schedule uploads. The runtime mode (Autopilot or Review-gated) is chosen here.
sections.why: Likely reason: extra files only apply to schedules, so they are hidden for packages. The meaning of the two modes is explained on screen rather than in the code.
sections.watch_out: The form does nothing if the file or documents are invalid. The disabled button and the message are the only feedback.

summary: The upload page where the user adds schedule, package or attachment files before analysis.
purpose: Lets the user add files by drag and drop or a picker, with checks before anything is sent.
why: Likely reason: checking files on the screen gives quick feedback and avoids sending unsuitable files.
how: Only the imports were visible. The steps for dropping, picking and checking files are not shown.
inputs: Files the user drops or chooses.
risks: The exact validation limits are in the uploadValidation file and were not visible here.
debug: If a file is rejected, read the messages from the validation helpers in uploadValidation.
